blindSummary: This is a small self-governing overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state; its economy is tourism-dependent and it is tiny. Same-sex acts were decriminalised in 2001 by a decree imposed from the administering state over the refusal of the local legislature; there is no legal recognition of same-sex partnerships.
blindOutOfScope: An overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations from the metropolitan norm are noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: this public-broadcaster article is about the administering state's own regional prison policy for trans inmates (a June 2026 ruling that guidance allowing some trans prisoners to be held in jails matching their gender identity is unlawful), not about this territory; it appears to have been included in the source list in error or as metropolitan-context material.

NOTE: this public-broadcaster article is about the same metropolitan-region prison-housing litigation (Feb 2026, suicide-risk arguments), not about this territory; included as metropolitan-context material only.

LGBT travel-news archive report (2012): a feature on gay life here - a quiet 35-square-mile island where homosexuality is virtually a non-issue: no visible community, organisations, Pride events or gay venues; gay life minimal and private; scattered gay-friendly hotel lounges exist.
A same-sex wedding-destination travel page: markets the island as a wedding/honeymoon destination with top beaches and a 'friendly, relaxed atmosphere' for same-sex couples.

Newswire via a legal-history site (Jan 2001): the metropolitan state scrapped homosexuality laws across five of its island territories by direct ruling from the metropolitan government after the local legislatures refused to act - decriminalising consensual same-sex acts in private; local religious leaders objected, calling it a cultural rift with the administering state.

Travel magazine (June 2023): first-person travel piece - a queer family visiting openly ('out and proud on a tiny island'); notes gay sex decriminalised since 2000 and explores whether LGBTQ travellers are welcome in practice.
